hyp_prompt:
ALERT: powershell.exe started with an -EncodedCommand argument on workstation WS-114.

INITIAL EVIDENCE:
- WS-114 is assigned to a user in the finance department
- No software deployment was scheduled for WS-114 today

CANDIDATE QUERIES (id: description [possible outcomes]):
- Q1: Identify the parent process of powershell.exe [office_application, management_agent, user_shell]
- Q2: Decode the encoded command and classify its content [download_and_execute, administrative_script, other]
- Q3: Check outbound connections from WS-114 in the 5 minutes after execution [unknown_external_host, internal_only, none]
- Q4: Count PowerShell executions on WS-114 in the past 30 days [frequent, rare]
- Q5: Check whether the logged-on user has local administrator rights [administrator, standard_user]

TASK: Generate 2-6 rival explanations, including at least one malicious and one benign explanation. Give each a prior probability (priors sum to 1). Then, for EVERY candidate query and EVERY hypothesis, give the probability of each listed outcome if that hypothesis were true (probabilities per query-hypothesis pair sum to 1). Use only the listed outcome names.

Respond by calling the report_hypotheses tool.

hypotheses.label: malicious
hypotheses.description: Phishing/macro-driven malicious payload: Office app spawns encoded PowerShell that downloads and executes a stager from an external host.

hypotheses.label: malicious
hypotheses.description: Hands-on-keyboard or post-compromise activity: attacker or malware launches encoded PowerShell from a user shell/script for discovery, persistence, or C2.

hypotheses.label: benign
hypotheses.description: Legitimate management agent or IT automation (e.g., SCCM, RMM, inventory) running an encoded administrative script outside scheduled deployment.

hypotheses.label: benign
hypotheses.description: Power user/admin or finance macro-savvy user running their own encoded script from a shell for routine automation.

select_raw.rationale: Decoding the command gives the strongest likelihood ratios between malicious (download_and_execute) and benign (administrative_script) hypotheses, and it also separates H1/H2 from H3/H4 better than the other queries.
